Exam Date & Time: 02-Jan-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
 THIRD SEMESTER B.Tech. (COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING) EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2024 / JANUARY  
  2025  
  SUBJECT: CSE 2123/CSE_2123 - DIGITAL SYSTEM DESIGN  
  (MAKEUP)  
  
  
  DIGITAL SYSTEM DESIGN [CSE 2123]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                         Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)                Design a synchronous sequential circuit for the following state diagram using JK Flip flop                 (5)  
  
  
1B)                Build the equations for low noise margin and high noise margin in logic circuits. Identify the terms       (3)  
  present in the equations. Identify the types of power dissipation in logic circuits.  
1C)                Simplify the following function using a 4-variable K-map, then implement the simplified expression         (2)  
  using only NAND gates.  
  
  
2A)                Explain the structure and working of a Full Adder.                                                         (5)  
  How does it differ from a Half Adder in being more suitable for multi-bit binary addition?  
2B)                Design and develop 4-bit carry-lookahead adder. Apply suitable approach to optimize the design to (3)  
  reduce the delay.  
2C)                Develop a 4-to-2 priority encoder using Verilog HDL. Implement the circuit and simulate its output         (2)  
  for different input combinations, ensuring that the highest priority input is encoded.  
3A)                Design a traffic light controller for a four-way intersection. The intersection allows two directions of   (5)  
  traffic: North-South (N-S) and East-West (E-W). To ensure safe passage, only one direction can  
  have a green light at a time. The controller must follow these rules:  
  
  Priority: The North-South direction has higher priority over the East-West direction.  
  
  
  Page 1 of 3

Traffic Requests: There are two sensors detecting vehicles waiting to cross in each direction:  
  SENSOR_NS is HIGH if there is traffic in the North-South direction. SENSOR_EW is HIGH if there  
  is traffic in the East-West direction. GREEN_NS and GREEN_EW are output signals that control  
  the green light for each direction: GREEN_NS goes HIGH to turn the green light on for the North-  
  South direction. GREEN_EW goes HIGH to turn the green light on for the East-West direction. If  
  both SENSOR _NS and SENSOR _EW are HIGH, GREEN_NS (North-South) should be HIGH due  
  to the priority rule, and GREEN_EW should stay LOW. When the green light is ON for a direction, it  
  should remain green until the traffic in that direction clears (i.e., the respective request signal goes  
  LOW).  
  
  Design an Finite State Machine for the Traffic Controller and synthesize it. Assume missing data/  
  conditions if any and state them.  
3B)   State the comparison between combinational and sequential circuits. Design a new flipflop whose            (3)  
  characteristics are given below, using T- flipflop.  
  
  
3C)   Draw an Algorithmic State Machine (ASM) chart to count the number of Ones present in a number              (2)  
  input to the system.  
4A)   Design a simple processor with a control circuitry that can perform the addition/subtraction of two 4- (5)  
  bit data. Provide suitable explanation.  
4B)   Design a 3-bit synchronous counter using D-flipflops that counts even states only and repeats the          (3)  
  sequence after reaching the maximum even number of the state. Consider the counter starts from  
  the '0' state. Assume unused states are don't cares.  
4C)   Write the Verilog behavioral description of a four-bit up-down counter with parallel load using three      (2)  
  control inputs for the three operations Load. Up, and Down. The order of precedence is Load, Up.  
  and Down.  
5A)   Since a computer has many registers, paths must be provided to transfer information from one               (5)  
  register to another. An efficient scheme for transferring the information between registers in a  
  multiple-register configuration is a common bus system. Design a 4-bit common bus system for 4-  
  registers of 4-bits each using multiplexers.  
5B)   Design a synchronous 3-bit up-down counter using JK-flipflops. Draw an appropriate sequence                (3)  
  diagram, excitation table, and logic diagram to realize the said counter.  
5C)   Determine the number of unused states and MOD of the following counter:                                    (2)
